newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 16.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Bolger keeps distance: Prime Minister Jim Bolger distanced himself on Thursday from Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters' refusal to apologise for assaulting National MP John Banks. Page 1.
Moore and Morris join super scheme backers: Youth Affairs Minister Deborah Morris on Thursday came out in favour of a compulsory superannuation scheme and was joined by Labour MP Mike Moore. Page 2.

Leap in jobless stirs opposition: Opposition parties called on Thursday for urgent action on reducing unemployment as the latest figures showed that falling economic growth had led to a sharp rise in the number of people out of work. Page 2.

Nats to air fears about coalition: The National Party's moves to distance itself from coalition partner NZ First will continue this weekend as it holds its Wellington and Canterbury-Westland regional conferences. Page 2.

BNZ moving strongly into new fields: The Bank of New Zealand is taking on the superannuation and insurance industry at its own game, lifting sales of super and life insurance products dramatically in the last six months. Page 10.

NZ tax too high -- US economist: Taxation in New Zealand as a share of gross domestic product was not shrinking despite last year's tax cuts, University of Texas economics professor Gerald Scully said on Thursday. Page 10.

FCL to buy employee trust shares: Fletcher Challenge's massive Employee Unit Trust, which controls 11.7 percent of the group's shares worth almost $900 million, is being wound back to just 2.7 percent. Page 10.

JeansWest undeterred in NZ: Sluggish retail sales in New Zealand have not deterred two Australian jeans chains from racing ahead with plans to catch sizable chunks of the local casual clothing market. Page 10.
Stefan's creator squeezed out: The Apple and Pear Marketing Board has shunted orange juice entrepreneur Stefan Lepionka out of a booming joint venture, citing a "difficult relationship". Page 11.
THE PRESS

Smith apologises to Aust: Agriculture Minister Lockwood Smith has privately apologised to his Australian counterpart John Anderson for the removal from a Melbourne park of fire blight-diseased specimens by a New Zealand scientist. Page 3.
CHH turns to staff on how to make money: The company is involving its 11,000 staff in ways of lifting productivity, finding new products, and increasing Asian sales. Page 16.
Mr Chips serves up higher div in spite of flat year: Mr Chips holdings has boosted its dividend in spite of the company reporting a static annual result on Thursday. Page 16.
No division at Apple Fields: Apple Fields shareholders voted without question on Thursday for the listed orchardist to become a property development company. Page 17.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Maine again asked for an explanation: Maine Investments copped its third stock exchange query in a month after Skellerup junk bonds soared to a 27 percent yield.
NZ-built bus the ticket for Thais: Thai commuters will soon be using buses designed and built in Manakau City, Auckland.

BNZ doubts 30pc profit lift will stay: The Bank of New Zealand says slower business conditions and continuing intense competition will make it difficult to retain a 30 percent rise in its first-half net profit in the second half.

Cultus results look good: Cultus Petroleum's wholly owned subsidiary Basin Oil NZ said on Thursday a preliminary core analysis undertaken in its WA-241-P joint-venture had produced highly encouraging results.
